findings.title: Backup code consumption is a non-atomic read-modify-write
findings.body: The user row is read at the start of authorize(). The code is then nulled out in memory, and the whole re-encrypted array is written back with an unconditional update. Two concurrent logins with the same backup code both read the unconsumed array and both succeed, which breaks the 'can be used exactly once' guarantee. Whichever write lands last also overwrites the other's changes, so a code consumed by one request can be restored by the other. Use a transaction or an optimistic check, for example update where backupCodes equals the value that was read, and fail if no row matched.

findings.title: Message tells users to generate backup codes in settings, but no such feature exists
findings.body: The `missing_backup_codes` string says "Please generate them in your settings". Backup codes are only generated inside the `/totp/setup` flow, and there is no regenerate option in settings. Existing users who already had 2FA enabled before this migration have `backupCodes = NULL`. They will see this message on 'Lost access' login or disable, with no way to act on it. If they have also lost their authenticator, they are locked out. Either add a regeneration path or change the message.

findings.title: Backup codes are lost if the dialog is dismissed on the codes step
findings.body: By the DisplayBackupCodes step, 2FA is already enabled on the server. The Dialog's `onOpenChange` is passed straight through and does not call `resetState()` or `onEnable()`. Pressing Esc or clicking the overlay therefore closes the modal without the user ever saving the codes, and the codes can never be shown again. It also leaves the step stuck at DisplayBackupCodes, so reopening the modal shows the old codes instead of restarting. Dismissal on this step should be blocked, or routed through the same close handler as the 'Close' button.

findings.title: E2E tests do not cover backup code login/disable; first test not updated for new step
findings.body: The PR says it fixes the 2FA setup test for the new backup-code screen. Only the 'disable' test was updated to close the backup-codes dialog. The 'enable and login' test never dismisses that dialog and works around it with a FIXME assertion that passes even when the switch is unchecked. The core new behaviours are untested: login with a backup code, single-use enforcement, and disabling with a backup code. Only a TODO comment mentions them.

findings.title: Clipboard write not awaited; success toast shown unconditionally
findings.body: `navigator.clipboard.writeText` returns a promise that can reject, for example without permission or on a non-secure context. The code ignores it and always shows 'Backup codes copied!'. A user may believe the codes were saved when they were not, and these are one-time-display secrets. Await the promise and show an error on failure.

findings.title: Password visibility toggle removed from keyboard tab order
findings.body: Adding `tabIndex={-1}` to the shared PasswordField toggle button makes it unreachable by keyboard. This regresses accessibility in every place PasswordField is used, not just the 2FA screens, and is unrelated to the feature.

findings.title: Unvalidated backupCode type can cause a 500
findings.body: `req.body.backupCode.replaceAll(...)` assumes a string. A non-string truthy value, such as a number or object, throws a TypeError and returns a 500 instead of a 400 IncorrectBackupCode. There is also no rate limiting on guesses against this endpoint, unlike the login path.
